notes: rk-nsex, THE TWO WAYS A REVIEW FAILS TO SAY VALID — one fixture, because they are one rule ('the verdict must be honestly VALID') and each is separately breakable. L1-1 carries a review whose `verdict` is INVALID, with a finding explaining why (the restatement drops the d-regularity hypothesis): the record still verifies mechanically, and is still not cite-able. L1-2 carries a review that says VALID while answering `hypotheses_complete: false` — the shape a rubber-stamp takes when the reviewer does the work, records the defect, and then ticks the box anyway. A verdict may not be more generous than the reviewer's own clauses, so the second is `[review-inconsistent]` rather than a pass. Both records' anchors verify (`4 anchors verified`) and neither is reviewed-VALID: mechanical anchoring and human judgement are separate coordinates and the coverage line reports them separately. `aism_behavior: n/a`. Mutation-proof: accepting any parseable review (dropping both the verdict test and the false-clause test) returns this fixture to zero findings, exit 0; dropping only the false-clause test leaves L1-1 red and L1-2 green, which is why both live here; observed and reverted.
